profile.headline: Experienced front-end and agentic engineer with deep TypeScript expertise, rich full-stack background, and a focus on LLM-driven approaches. Passionate about thoughtful, scalable user experiences, teaching, open source.
profile.summary:
I’ve been building for the web for over two decades. I started coding before I ever stepped into a college classroom—tinkering with BASIC on my dad’s old Atari I found buried in a closet, building websites for my family’s bookstore in the Bahamas, and writing Perl scripts to search text files. That early sense of curiosity never left me.

Professionally, I’ve spent most of my career focused on front-end development, with a specialization in JavaScript and TypeScript. From the rise of AJAX to the evolution of modern frameworks, I’ve been hands-on through every wave. I’ve contributed to major open source projects like the Dojo Toolkit and WordPress, helped maintain public-facing codebases, and collaborated with engineers across the globe.

But I’ve never been just a front-end developer. I have strong full-stack experience as well—building POS systems, crafting server-side solutions in PHP, Node, and Java, optimizing complex data flows, and solving performance issues that directly affected thousands of users. I’ve worked in startups, in government, at established remote-first companies, and independently.

Alongside shipping code, I’ve done a lot of teaching—from internal team mentorship to running multi-day training sessions for developer teams across industries. I’ve also been a podcast host, sharing deep dives into TypeScript, architecture decisions, and patterns that make code more durable and developer-friendly.

More recently, I’ve turned my focus toward the rapidly unfolding world of AI and large language models—especially how they intersect with code generation, systematizing domain knowledge, and enabling new forms of creative tooling. I’m building workflows, products, and experiments that use LLMs to make experts more expressive, not replace them.

My approach to technology is grounded in empathy, utility, and sustainability. I care deeply about fairness in pricing, clarity in UX, and giving people tools that make them feel more capable, not more confused.

I’m especially interested in opportunities where I can:
	•	Build or improve complex web applications with meaningful user impact
	•	Collaborate on LLM-powered tools that empower developers or creators
	•	Contribute to open source projects with long-term value
	•	Join thoughtful teams that value authenticity and craft

If that resonates—or you’re just curious about the work I’m doing—I’d love to connect.

positions.title: Professional development
positions.description:
After accepting an “alignment offer” with severance from Automattic, I took the opportunity to step back, reassess, and invest deeply in both my technical growth and the kinds of products I’ve always wanted to build.

Although I was hired at Automattic as a JavaScript engineer, much of my time there was spent on backend PHP work. Once I left, I committed to catching up on the modern JavaScript ecosystem—diving into React, TypeScript, and newer tools and patterns that had gained traction like Remix and TanStack Start.

I became deeply immersed in the world of large language models (LLMs), with a strong focus on prompt engineering, generative coding, and agentic frameworks. I’ve explored and built with platforms like LangGraph, DSPy, and Mastra, studying how LLMs can augment not just developer workflows but also creative and complex systems across industries.

In parallel, I improved several of my live projects, including a pairwise ranking engine and a Disney dining search tool. I also began developing new, original applications. One of my most ambitious current projects is a faithful digital implementation of the analog Bullet Journal system. To bring it to life, I’ve become proficient in React Native, and I architected a custom sync engine using Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects.

I’ve also explored modern data tooling—experimenting with Drizzle, Prisma, and ultimately choosing TinyBase for this project due to its flexibility and performance for local-first apps.

This break has allowed me to grow more than any structured role ever could. I’ve reconnected with what I love about building software: solving problems with empathy, curiosity, and deep technical focus. I’m now better equipped—technically and creatively—to bring useful, human-centered tools to market.

positions.title: Javascript Engineer
positions.description:
I worked across multiple teams with a focus on building and improving the systems that help millions of users get paid and keep their sites running.

I started on Team Shilling, where I was responsible for the checkout, payments, billing, and account management systems that power WordPress.com checkout. My work involved refining the Stripe integration, managing complex subscription and renewal logic, handling transactional system errors, and ensuring users had a smooth and reliable experience from first purchase through billing cycles.

One of my proudest accomplishments was resolving a long-standing issue where connecting a Stripe account to multiple WordPress.com sites would break the payment flow entirely. The fix not only restored functionality for those users—it directly impacted their ability to earn income, and was a great example of meaningful, user-centered problem-solving.

Later, I joined Team Gold, where I shifted focus to building and maintaining monetization tools—the systems that allow users to turn their content into sustainable businesses. This included new features and backend logic that supported ads, premium subscriptions, and other monetization strategies for creators and publishers using the WordPress.com platform.

Although I was hired primarily for my JavaScript and TypeScript expertise, I worked extensively with PHP and server-side logic throughout my time at Automattic. I also contributed to WordPress Core and the Calypso project, collaborating across teams to address user-facing bugs and infrastructure issues that spanned multiple layers of the stack.

My time at Automattic deepened my interest in performance, reliability, and building systems that not only scale—but support users in tangible, real-world ways.
positions.insights: Skills: React.js · TypeScript · Node.js · Stripe Connect · PHP

positions.title: Commiter
positions.description:
During my time contributing to the Dojo Toolkit, I worked on both Dojo 1 and Dojo 2, with a particular focus on widget tooling, developer experience, and internal documentation systems.

I collaborated on the early widgeting infrastructure, which powered core UI components and enabled developer extensibility. My work spanned architectural decisions and practical implementation. 

One of my most notable contributions was building the inline code system we used to document the API. I developed the parser and frontend interface used to display our documentation, enabling a smoother onboarding and reference experience for both contributors and consumers of the toolkit.

I authored and maintained the first implementation of the Django Template Language in JavaScript, adapting server-side rendering patterns to client-side applications and helping bridge gaps between front-end and back-end mental models at the time.

Throughout my involvement, I collaborated closely with other core contributors—participating in frequent in-person meetups, architectural reviews, and collaborative design sessions. This experience helped refine not only my JavaScript and TypeScript expertise but also how I approach large-scale open source work.

Dojo gave me a foundation in thoughtful, scalable front-end engineering and a deep appreciation for developer tooling and community-driven design.
positions.insights: Skills: JavaScript · TypeScript · AJAX Frameworks · Documentation · Architectural Design

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
When I returned to SitePen, the front-end landscape was beginning to shift in two major ways: TypeScript was gaining traction, and reactive programming was starting to change how web apps were built. I leaned into both of these developments early. I became fluent in TypeScript at a time when few engineers had adopted it, and we quickly embraced it across SitePen projects to increase maintainability and catch issues earlier in development.

I was also involved in the development of Dojo 2, providing early feedback on its direction and working on some of the initial widgets it launched with. While my involvement in core development was lighter than in the Dojo 1 era, I remained closely engaged in how the framework evolved and was applied in client projects.

This time around, my role included much heavier client-facing engineering. I worked on several complex, high-stakes projects, including enterprise customers in hospitality, financial services, and banking.

These projects deepened my ability to work within enterprise environments, understand client needs, and build front-end systems that were modernization of, in many cases, brittle and poorly understood codebases. My experience with these projects helped fuel my love of spelunking and untangling complicated systems.

Throughout this period, I continued to represent SitePen through training, internal mentoring, and co-hosting a TypeScript-focused podcast, helping the broader community understand emerging best practices in modern JavaScript and TypeScript development.
positions.insights: Skills: TypeScript · Dojo · Debugging · Enterprise Software · Systems Engineering

positions.title: Co-Founder & Programmer
positions.description:
I founded this company with a friend I met through the co-working space he was launching. During my time here, I moved from hands-on enterprise training to full-scale product development. Early on, we continued the momentum I had built at SitePen by conducting on-site technical training for clients, focusing on modern web development practices and tooling.

Our first major project was a real estate platform built in Python with Django, using PostGIS  for location-based search.

As mobile development exploded, we shifted focus to iOS and Android. I wrote the first version of the BNO News app, one of the earliest apps to make full use of Apple’s newly released push notification system. We designed a custom opt-in alert system that allowed users to subscribe to categorized, real-time news updates—a novel concept at the time.

One of our largest client projects was for SmartyPig, a consumer savings platform. We built and launched fully-featured iOS and Android apps that mirrored the website’s functionality, including full account management, goal tracking, and transactional tools. These apps required careful coordination between user experience, mobile limitations, and financial APIs to deliver a smooth, secure interface for customers managing real money.

A long-running project was the official app for the 80/35 Music Festival, which we maintained for five consecutive years. The app included a performance schedule, interactive venue map, and tools for users to build personalized festival lineups. We tailored the app annually to accommodate lineup changes, user feedback, and design updates.

This period gave me deep experience in full-stack development, early mobile systems, and product delivery under startup constraints. I was the sole developer and was responsible for implementing all aspects of our applications. It strengthened my perspective on how to translate business needs into reliable, user-focused software across platforms.
positions.insights: Skills: iOS Development · Android Development · Python · Geographic Information Systems (GIS) · PostgreSQL

positions.title: Co-Founder & Programmer
positions.description:
At BitMethod, we eventually pivoted to work full-time on Change, one of the early mobile-based point-of-sale systems, built in close collaboration with several local restaurants. The system featured flexible order and modifier management, with a strong focus on tracking adjustments to common menu items—tailored specifically to real-world restaurant workflows.

I built a custom ORM layer on top of the iOS frameworks available at the time, allowing for synchronization and complex, reusable object queries and consistent references regardless of how records were retrieved. This abstraction made the system highly adaptable and performant, remaining in memory for months without crashing.

Additional features included receipt printer integration, emailed receipts, and direct integration with payment processors, all tightly woven into the app’s flow to reduce friction for staff and customers alike.
positions.insights: Skills: iOS Development · Customer Support · ORM Tools · Payment Card Processing · Data Synchronization

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
During my first tenure at SitePen, I focused heavily on JavaScript-based front-end development and on-site technical training. I led many week-long, in-person training sessions for enterprise teams, creating all the accompanying instructional materials and guiding developers through hands-on learning. This work helped lay a foundation for better tooling and developer confidence in large-scale JavaScript adoption at the time.

To support these sessions, I developed an interactive assignment tool that let attendees experiment with code examples in a guided, iterative way—one of the early precursors to what we now think of as in-browser learning environments.

Beyond training, I contributed to several client projects. One standout involved building a web-based user interface for managing ad campaigns, including the logic and interactions needed for ad targeting and placement. This was a complex UI, designed to help non-technical users configure detailed ad parameters effectively.

This period shaped my early experience in scaling JavaScript to real-world applications, emphasizing clarity, usability, and developer empowerment long before the modern JS ecosystem matured.
positions.insights: Skills: JavaScript · Training · Teaching · Enterprise Software

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: I worked on data aggregation, deduplication, and cleanup across multiple DoD health record systems, primarily in Java. Deployment restrictions led to heavy use of JavaScript, which sparked my deeper involvement in front-end development. This was a highly engineering-centric environment—with rigorous code reviews, pair programming, and detailed QA processes. I also focused extensively on introducing robust debugging tools and logging, improving the reliability and traceability of legacy code.
positions.insights: Skills: Java · Debugging · QA Engineering · Pair Programming · Code Review

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
The company produces magazines that are customizable through a web interface that allows real estate agents to keep in contact with their clients by branding their magazine to their company/agent.

I worked in PHP on internal and external customer management tools, adapting an open source CRM to fit our needs while preserving compatibility for the broader community. I performed extensive data scraping using regular expressions, XPath, and DOM traversal, ultimately building a database of over 300,000 real estate agents.

I supported the sales team directly as a key technical resource and contributed articles and editorial content to the company’s magazine.
positions.insights: Skills: Writing · Web Scraping · Regular Expressions · Customer Relationship Management (CRM) · PHP

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: As a summer intern, I developed the marketing site for a new wireless VoIP telephony service the company was launching. In addition to web design, I was hands-on with site surveillance setup, antenna installation, and telephony systems configuration, supporting both the digital and physical infrastructure for the service rollout.
positions.insights: Skills: HTML · CSS · Topographic Surveys · Field Installation · Network Installation

positions.title: Technical Support Technician
positions.description: During my summer internship at, I handled call triage and diagnostics, gaining hands-on experience with node management and issue resolution. I created scripts to speed up troubleshooting and developed an interactive diagnostic flowchart that became a reusable tool for support teams to more quickly identify and resolve service issues.
positions.insights: Skills: Cable Modems · Customer Support · Customer Service · Hardware Diagnostics · Employee Training

projects.title: Rank Duel
projects.description:
Pairwise ranking supporting arbitrary data through a JSON import (Disney World restaurants shown here).

Uses a directed acyclic graph (DAG) for exhaustive ranking, combined with TrueSkill ranking for in-progress sorting and targeted comparisons. Performs similarly to general purpose sorting algorithms but allows flexibility by avoiding recency and allowing skipping.

When I returned to SitePen, the front-end landscape was beginning to shift in two major ways: TypeScript was gaining traction, and reactive programming was starting to change how web apps were built. I leaned into both of these developments early. I became fluent in TypeScript at a time when few engineers had adopted it, and we quickly embraced it across SitePen projects to increase maintainability and catch issues earlier in development.

I was also involved in the development of Dojo 2, providing early feedback on its direction and working on some of the initial widgets it launched with. While my involvement in core development was lighter than in the Dojo 1 era, I remained closely engaged in how the framework evolved and was applied in client projects.

This time around, my role included much heavier client-facing engineering. I worked on several complex, high-stakes projects, including enterprise customers in hospitality, financial services, and banking.

These projects deepened my ability to work within enterprise environments, understand client needs, and build front-end systems that were modernization of, in many cases, brittle and poorly understood codebases. My experience with these projects helped fuel my love of spelunking and untangling complicated systems.

Throughout this period, I continued to represent SitePen through training, internal mentoring, and co-hosting a TypeScript-focused podcast, helping the broader community understand emerging best practices in modern JavaScript and TypeScript development.

experience.title: Co-Founder & Programmer
experience.description:
I founded this company with a friend I met through the co-working space he was launching. During my time here, I moved from hands-on enterprise training to full-scale product development. Early on, we continued the momentum I had built at SitePen by conducting on-site technical training for clients, focusing on modern web development practices and tooling.

Our first major project was a real estate platform built in Python with Django, using PostGIS  for location-based search.

As mobile development exploded, we shifted focus to iOS and Android. I wrote the first version of the BNO News app, one of the earliest apps to make full use of Apple’s newly released push notification system. We designed a custom opt-in alert system that allowed users to subscribe to categorized, real-time news updates—a novel concept at the time.

One of our largest client projects was for SmartyPig, a consumer savings platform. We built and launched fully-featured iOS and Android apps that mirrored the website’s functionality, including full account management, goal tracking, and transactional tools. These apps required careful coordination between user experience, mobile limitations, and financial APIs to deliver a smooth, secure interface for customers managing real money.

A long-running project was the official app for the 80/35 Music Festival, which we maintained for five consecutive years. The app included a performance schedule, interactive venue map, and tools for users to build personalized festival lineups. We tailored the app annually to accommodate lineup changes, user feedback, and design updates.

This period gave me deep experience in full-stack development, early mobile systems, and product delivery under startup constraints. I was the sole developer and was responsible for implementing all aspects of our applications. It strengthened my perspective on how to translate business needs into reliable, user-focused software across platforms.
experience.insights: Skills: iOS Development · Android Development · Python · Geographic Information Systems (GIS) · PostgreSQL

experience.title: Co-Founder & Programmer
experience.description:
At BitMethod, we eventually pivoted to work full-time on Change, one of the early mobile-based point-of-sale systems, built in close collaboration with several local restaurants. The system featured flexible order and modifier management, with a strong focus on tracking adjustments to common menu items—tailored specifically to real-world restaurant workflows.

I built a custom ORM layer on top of the iOS frameworks available at the time, allowing for synchronization and complex, reusable object queries and consistent references regardless of how records were retrieved. This abstraction made the system highly adaptable and performant, remaining in memory for months without crashing.

Additional features included receipt printer integration, emailed receipts, and direct integration with payment processors, all tightly woven into the app’s flow to reduce friction for staff and customers alike.
